calls.reason: The evidence is mixed. One blogger's tests found failed and unusable outputs, while Tom's Guide found the agent useful for everyday tasks. Neither measures how much usefulness errors actually cost.
This is an open-ended 'eventually' forecast. The only evidence is a St. Louis Fed estimate of general AI time savings from before the forecast, which neither settles it nor contradicts it.

At launch, Altman warned against using the agent for high-stakes or personal tasks, and the agent was built to refuse bank transfers. CRMArena-Pro found about 35% success on multi-turn tasks. Big Tech capex of several hundred billion fits the investment framing.
Capgemini's April 2025 survey shows trust falling from a 2024 baseline. Nothing in the packet compares customer disappointment in March with late July 2025.

The best agent in CMU's benchmark completed 24% of tasks, and a July tester found plenty of simple failures. Even Tom's Guide's positive review says you need to step in and restart, and its successes fit the narrow-use exception.

The share is explicitly a guess. The only aggregate figure is $340M over 2024-25 from a low-quality market report, set against about $193B in AI venture funding. That points below 1% but is too weak to call.
